question: On 17 December 2025, the Commission brought forward a proposal for a regulation establishing a temporary decarbonisation fund.

The aim is for the fund – during the period 2028-2029 – to provide temporary support to EU producers of selected CBAM goods in order to mitigate the risk of CO₂ leakage, as well as to counter the loss of competitiveness in thirdcountry markets where EU products might be being displaced by cheaper, more emissionintensive alternatives.

While the CBAM has been in force for a number of basic goods since the beginning of the year, it has been noted that CO₂-intensive semi-finished goods higher up the value chain are not covered until 1 January 2028. This could create distortions of competition to the detriment of EU producers and suppliers who make a living from processing basic goods into semifinished products for further production.
With that in mind: 1.
Can the Commission explain why CO₂-intensive semi-finished products will not be covered by the CBAM until 1 January 2028, and provide the assessments that formed the basis for that decision?
Can the Commission indicate whether and how the decarbonisation fund can be used to support companies exposed to distortions of competition from third-country products in the intervening period?
Has the Commission assessed the possibilities of making semi-finished products subject to CBAM before 1 January 2028 in order to address the distortion of competition that is currently taking place?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.4.2026) The Commission proposed on 17 December 2025 to extend the scope of the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) to selected steel and aluminium-intensive downstream goods. This scope extension covers intermediate goods and final goods and aims to address the risk of downstream carbon leakage.

The Commission has proposed an entry into force date of 1 January 2028 for the downstream extension. This allows time for the legislative process and subsequently for developing and amending the relevant implementing acts. Furthermore, it allows all stakeholders involved, including importers, national authorities and third country producers, sufficient time to prepare for the downstream extension.

The Temporary Decarbonisation Fund is an environmental measure. It will provide support to EU producers of certain CBAM goods to reduce their exposure to a remaining carbon leakage risk. Support will be granted for the production years 2026 and 2027. EU producers will have to demonstrate decarbonisation efforts to receive support.

The forthcoming EU Emission Trading System (ETS) review will provide the opportunity for a comprehensive review of how best to address the issue of the remaining risk of carbon leakage from 2028 onwards. It should be recalled that that the CBAM is phased-in gradually, meaning that there is only a small reduction in installations’ free allocation in 2026 and 2027 for the production of goods in scope of CBAM (2.

5% and 5% respectively). The transitory character of the Fund precludes any interpretation that it may constitute a precedent, a model or a reference point for the EU ETS review. Accordingly, the existence, operation or cessation of the Fund shall not create any expectation, legal or otherwise, regarding the EU ETS review.
